Standardise a variable or scale it to a percentage

Source: R/std.R
std.Rd

Vector helpers for dplyr::mutate(), following Stata's egen:

  • std() standardises to mean 0 and standard deviation 1, like egen z = std(x). Unlike scale(), it returns a plain vector.

  • pc() gives each value as a percentage of the total, like egen p = pc(x), or as a proportion with prop = TRUE.

Usage

std(x, mean = 0, sd = 1)

pc(x, prop = FALSE)

pct(x, prop = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A numeric or logical vector. Labelled numeric vectors are used through their codes.

mean, sd

The mean and standard deviation of the result, like Stata's egen std(x), mean() std() options.

prop

A single TRUE or FALSE. If TRUE, pc() returns proportions (summing to 1) instead of percentages (summing to 100).

Value

A double vector the same length as x. Missing values stay missing. std() returns all NA when the standard deviation is zero or undefined (fewer than two observed values), and pc() when the total is zero, as Stata gives missing values there.

Details

pct() is an alias of pc(). The gt package also exports a pct() (for column widths), so prefer pc() when gt is attached. In grouped dplyr::mutate() (or with .by), the mean, standard deviation and total come from each group, like Stata's by g: egen.

See also

Other variable generation functions: as_dummy(), cut, panel, row_egen

Examples

std(c(1, 2, 3, NA))
#> [1] -1  0  1 NA
pc(c(2, 3, 5))
#> [1] 20 30 50
pc(c(2, 3, 5), prop = TRUE)
#> [1] 0.2 0.3 0.5

lifeexp |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    z = std(lexp),
    share = pc(popgrowth),
    .by = region
  )
#> # A tibble: 68 × 8
